raw_response:
Well, I've been farming these 8 mu for 55 years now, since I was 13 years old. I only went to primary school, but my father taught me everything about this land, and I've watched what works with my own eyes. Now it's just me and my wife at home — we're both getting old, and the children are working in Shijiazhuang. They send a little money, but not much. I have to make do with what the land gives me.

I split my 8 mu into two parts. Five mu I do wheat then maize, that's the main thing that feeds us. Three mu I plant cotton for extra cash. I know cotton is a lot of work, especially in September when it overlaps with maize harvest, but I've been doing it for twenty years. Old Wang down the road does the same, and his cotton always looks good.

The wheat I planted last October is looking okay — not the best I've seen, but not bad either. We had some rain in early spring. Before planting, I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, same as always. In March when the wheat was jointing, I topdressed about half a bag of urea per mu. Now it's late April, the wheat is heading. I'll irrigate it one more time before harvest in early June if the weather stays dry — the well water costs money, metered by the village, so I don't water more than I have to. Maybe one more spray for aphids. I expect about 400 kg per mu this year, same as last year. I saved my own seed, so no seed cost.

For cotton, I'm planting right now. I save my own seed from last year — buying new hybrid seed is too expensive, and my seed has done fine. I'll till the 3 mu with the small tractor, put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, then plant by hand. Cotton needs spraying, that's for sure. The bollworms always come in July and August. I'll spray four or five times this season, herbicide and insecticide mainly. I'll water twice, once after planting to help it settle, and once when it's flowering in July. The old lady helps with picking — it's hard on our backs, kneeling in the field, but what can we do? I hope for about 250 kg of lint per mu.

The tricky part is June. As soon as I cut the wheat, I have to get the maize in the ground. The window is maybe five days, no more. If it rains, the soil gets heavy and I'm in trouble. I usually hire the neighbor with the tractor-planter to help — costs me about 100 yuan, but it's worth it. Maize seed I have to buy, it's hybrid, about 60 yuan per mu. When planting, I put fertilizer in the hole, about 40 kg of compound per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high, around late July, I'll topdress some urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. Water twice if the summer is dry — once in July, once in August. I expect around 420 kg per mu if things go normal.

Money is always tight. I'm watching every yuan. I thought about putting more fertilizer on the wheat this year, but then I thought — what if one of us gets sick? I need to keep some cash in my pocket. So I'll do about the same as last year. That's my plan. You don't change what works when you're my age, and you don't gamble with money you don't have.
